question: Told that 2-4-6 fits a hidden rule, people propose their own triples to test guesses. Why do most announce a wrong rule?
options: They test only triples their guess allows
The hidden rule is too complex to guess
They are allowed too few test triples
answer: They test only triples their guess allows. The rule was simply any three rising numbers, so a guess like even numbers going up by two keeps earning yeses. Only a triple the guess forbids, such as 1-2-3, could expose it. Seeking yeses often works; it fails when the truth is broader than the guess.
move: When every test says yes, ask whether a broader rule would say yes too.
trap: Assuming people fail because the hidden rule must be complicated.
source: Wason, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 1960
reference: Wason, On the failure to eliminate hypotheses in a conceptual task, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 1960
